name: Avial
equipment: Heavy pan or kadai with a lid: cooks the vegetables and holds the finished avial
Small mixer-grinder jar (or mortar and pestle): for the coarse coconut paste
Chopping board, sharp knife, measuring spoons, kitchen scale, a small bowl and a fork or whisk for the curd
A fork or knife tip to test the vegetables

steps.title: Peel and cut the yam
steps.text: Peel 40 g yam and cut it into strips about 5 cm long and 1 cm thick.
steps.visualCue: Even pale strips, all about the length of your little finger
steps.cameraCheck: The yam strips on the board
steps.videoShot: Knife slicing a yam slab into strips.
steps.watchOut: Itchy hands from the raw yam (rub a little oil on your hands first or wear gloves; rinse with water if it itches), and uneven strips, which cook unevenly; re-cut the thick ones to match.

steps.title: Peel and cut the raw plantain
steps.text: Peel 40 g raw plantain (rub a little oil on the knife, as the sap can stain) and cut it into strips the same size as the yam.
steps.visualCue: Pale cream strips, the same size as the yam
steps.cameraCheck: Plantain and yam strips side by side
steps.videoShot: Peeling the green skin off the plantain.
steps.watchOut: Strips that turn brown if left out; drop them into a bowl of water until you cook, then drain.

steps.title: Cut the carrot, beans and drumstick
steps.text: Cut 25 g carrot into strips like the yam, 25 g beans into 5 cm pieces, and the drumstick into 5 cm pieces. Keep the beans in a separate bowl.
steps.visualCue: Every vegetable about the same length, about 5 cm
steps.cameraCheck: All the cut vegetables, beans in a separate bowl
steps.videoShot: Drumstick pieces dropping into a bowl.
steps.watchOut: Cutting the beans too short, so they turn limp; keep them the same length as the other strips.

steps.title: Make the coconut paste
steps.text: Put 30 g grated coconut, 4 g green chilli, 1 g cumin and 10 ml water in a small jar. Pulse 3-4 times, in short bursts.
steps.visualCue: A coarse, damp, crumbly paste with visible coconut specks, not a smooth purée
steps.cameraCheck: The coarse paste, shown in the jar
steps.videoShot: Pulsing the jar and tipping out the coarse paste.
steps.watchOut: Over-grinding into a smooth, watery paste, which makes the avial runny (Veg Recipes of India says to keep the paste coarse); if that happens, simmer 1-2 min longer in step 10.

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Put 40 g (3 tbsp) curd in a small bowl and whisk until smooth.
steps.cameraCheck: The whisked curd in the bowl
steps.watchOut: Cold curd straight from the fridge going into a hot pan, which can split it; keep it on the counter while you cook the vegetables.

steps.title: Start the firm vegetables
steps.text: Put the yam, plantain, carrot and drumstick in the pan. Add 0.5 g (¼ tsp) turmeric, 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt and 60 ml water.
steps.visualCue: The strips sit half-covered by yellow water
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with vegetables and yellow water
steps.watchOut: Too much water, which dilutes the final dish; use only 60 ml here, the vegetables also release water.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover, bring to a gentle boil on medium heat, then simmer for 8 min.
steps.visualCue: Steam under the lid; the yam and plantain edges look slightly translucent
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan with steam at the edge
steps.watchOut: The pan drying out and the vegetables sticking; if you hear sizzling, add 2 tbsp water at once.

steps.title: Add the beans
steps.text: Add the 25 g beans, cover and cook 4 min more.
steps.visualCue: The beans stay bright green, not olive
steps.watchOut: Beans that turn dull and soft from cooking too long; add them late and test at 3 min.

steps.title: Test the vegetables
steps.text: Push a fork into the yam and the plantain.
steps.tip: Yam takes the longest, so judge doneness by the yam.
steps.visualCue: The fork goes in with light resistance, and the strips still keep their shape
steps.cameraCheck: A fork piercing a yam strip
steps.videoShot: Fork sinking into a yam strip.
steps.watchOut: Raw, hard yam (cook 2-3 min more) or mush (too long; stir gently and move to the next step).

steps.title: Add the coconut paste
steps.text: Add the coarse coconut paste on top. Stir gently with a spoon, then cover and cook on low for 3 min.
steps.visualCue: The paste coats the vegetables and the smell turns from raw coconut to sweet and warm; most of the watery liquid is gone
steps.videoShot: Paste being spread over the vegetables.
steps.watchOut: Stirring hard so the strips break; fold gently or just shake the pan.

steps.title: Add the curd
steps.text: Turn the heat to low and add the whisked curd. Stir gently for 1 min, until it warms through. Do not boil.
steps.visualCue: The curd turns the coating creamy off-white and thick, and clings to the vegetables
steps.cameraCheck: The creamy coating in the pan
steps.watchOut: Boiling hard, which splits the curd into grains and water; if it curdles, switch off the heat and stir in 1 tbsp warm water.

steps.title: Finish with oil and curry leaves
steps.text: Switch off the heat. Drizzle 5 g (1 tsp) raw coconut oil on top and add 10 curry leaves. Cover and rest 5 min, then taste and add a pinch of salt only if needed.
steps.visualCue: A glossy sheen on top and a strong coconut oil and curry leaf smell when you lift the lid
steps.cameraCheck: The finished avial in the pan
steps.videoShot: Oil being drizzled over the finished avial.
steps.watchOut: Adding the oil in the hot pan on the flame, which dulls the smell; add it after the heat is off. If it tastes flat, a pinch of salt fixes it.
steps.funFact: Avial is often the star dish of a traditional Kerala sadhya feast (English Wikipedia's Avial article).

reasons: five vegetables in one bowl, no frying, only 5 g oil, no added sugar and about 7 g of fibre, with no cholesterol worries (about 5 mg). Points off for saturated fat of about 14 g (about 64% of a daily limit, nearly all from coconut and coconut oil), sodium of about 650 mg and low protein (about 5 g). Restaurant versions commonly add more coconut and oil and more salt, and are served with white rice in a sadya, so a bowl of 350 kcal or more with more saturated fat is likely (est.).

researchRating.basis: a very widely published Kerala classic, a standard of the sadya feast and described by Veg Recipes of India, Sharmi's Passions, Archana's Kitchen, Cook Click N Devour, Onmanorama and Scroll as the coconut-and-curd vegetable curry that goes with rice. Points off because recipes vary (curd, raw mango or tamarind; which vegetables), yam and plantain can be hard to find outside Kerala, and it is rarely sold as a delivery dish. Recipe-site star counts were not checked this run. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour). Freezing is not recommended: the curd and coconut coating can split on thawing and the yam turns grainy. Reheat in a pan on low heat with 1-2 tbsp water, stirring gently until just warm; do not boil hard, or the curd may split.
leftoverRemix: Avial paratha stuffing. Mash the leftover avial well, cook it down until almost dry, and use it as the filling for a plain whole-wheat paratha or toasted wrap, with a little green chutney.
burnOff: about 4.1 km of running (290 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 5.8 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 10 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 1 cup rice (about 490 kcal): about 7 km running or 9.8 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: table salt and curry leaf-and-cumin tempering are fine, but use sendha namak and cook only the commonly allowed vegetables (raw plantain, yam, drumstick if your family eats it); leave out carrot and beans (assumption: the common rule set; families differ).

ekadashi.reason: no grain and no onion or garlic, but beans are a legume under the common rule set; cook only yam, raw plantain, drumstick and coconut with sendha namak (families differ).

jain.reason: yam and carrot are roots; use the Jain variant (raw plantain and extra beans instead). No onion, garlic or hing in the main recipe.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; moderate sodium (about 650 mg) and not heavy, a good side with rice at iftar dinner or with rice or appam at sehri.

jain.reason: fresh yam and carrot are roots; swap yam for more raw plantain and carrot for more beans (see Jain variant). No onion, garlic or hing in the main recipe.

vegan.reason: the main recipe uses curd (40 g); use raw mango or tamarind for the sourness (see Vegan variant).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian recipe with no meat or egg.

sattvik.reason: the main recipe has no onion or garlic.

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava, maida or hing in the main recipe; if you add hing, use gluten-free hing because most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour.

dairyFree.reason: curd; use the dairy-free (raw mango) version, or coconut yoghurt (see Diet variants).
